the spectral shape of DOM is strongly related to acidity and less strongly to latitude and retention time.
the spectral absorbance metrics are sensitive indicators of acidity, and that they are also influenced by latitude.
the specific absorbance of DOM is higher at lower pH, and higher at lower latitude, and that the spectral slope of DOM is lower at lower pH, but higher at lower latitude.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specific absorbance of DOM in boreal lakes decreases with acidity and increases with latitude.
absorbance spectroscopy, as a tool for describing DOM quality, is most useful for comparing lakes with similar acidity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
spectral metrics should be interpreted cautiously, especially when they are used in conjunction with one another.
spectral absorbance metrics are sensitive to the acidity and retention-time of the lakes sampled.
